fields.name: clinician_confirmed_same_date_order
fields.label: Clinician confirmed same date order
fields.rule: **C; human-entered; required when and only when two or more non-deleted `DEVICE_LEAD_STATUS_EVENTS` rows for this `lead_id` share this `status_effective_date`, and rejected as an ERROR when this event is the only one for the lead on that date.** It is the clinician's statement of **what actually happened first**, expressed as a relative rank among that date's events for that lead. **Necessity:** without it the server has no source of intra-day chronology at all, and v1.3 inferred order from severity — which reconstructs the real sequence `NORMAL → FAILED → NORMAL after successful revision` as a lead that ended FAILED, corrupting the Section 1.4 lead-survival endpoint in exactly the cases that matter. No other stored field can supply this: severity, disposition, source type, and insertion order are all independent of time. **Burden effect:** zero on the Section 10.5 reference pathway, which contains no lead; and zero on the ordinary single-event lead day, where the field is rejected and the server assigns 1 automatically. It costs one entry per event only on a day when several events for one lead genuinely occurred, which is the day whose order cannot otherwise be known. **Audited:** the mutation that writes or corrects this field requires a `reason` and records `clinician_confirmed_same_date_order` in `ACTIVITY_LOG.changed_field_codes`, so the confirmed order is attributable and reviewable. Ties are rejected: two events for one lead and date may not carry the same value
